messages:
maria: Heads up — planning final GA gate for dedicated billing + SLA exceptions. Need a quick sync on SLA targets, billing/proration rules for reserved capacity, docs checklist, support routing/oncall, and the SLA credits process. Who can pick up the initial checklist?

ajay: I can draft SLA bullets today. Quick question: do we standardize on p95 or p99 for latency SLOs? Runtime numbers vary a lot by model size. For small models we currently see ~20ms p95 locally but hosted is higher.

sophie: DevEx/docs here — we need at minimum: pricing matrix (tiers vs reserved capacity), billing examples (proration, overage), FAQs, and copy for "What counts as downtime". Also need exact language for data residency/private deployments.

kevin: Support & oncall notes: propose routing: initial triage to #support-dedicated (L1), escalate to #eng-oncall after 15m for P1. Need runbooks for common P1s (node OOM, model stuck in compile, KV cache corruption). Also we should spell out SLA credit request flow (who validates, timeline). @maria can sales approve short-circuit?

lili: Legal: SLA credits need a clear formula and cap. Draft proposal: credit_pct = min(50, (downtime_minutes / total_month_minutes) * 100) — capped at 50%. Need to confirm with finance and compliance for regulatory customers.

ajay: Two more items that affect SLOs: region fallback and model variant fallback. We should define "available" precisely (e.g., successful response from requested region within X ms without automatic fallback) or call out fallbacks as separate behavior. Also, streaming responses introduce different latency metrics.

maria: Suggested action items: 1) Ajay — SLA bullets + definition of "available" 2) Sophie — pricing matrix skeleton + billing examples 3) Kevin — runbooks + channel routing doc 4) Lili — legal wording + credit formula and cap 5) Maria (me) — sync with sales on pricing tiers and enterprise exceptions. Can we commit to draft versions by EOD Friday?

ajay: Yes, I'll push a short RFC by tomorrow afternoon. Will include a proposed SLA table:

```
SLA Tier | p95 latency | p99 latency | availability definition
Hosted Standard | 300ms | 800ms | <5% fallback, successful inference within 800ms
Dedicated Bronze | 200ms | 600ms | dedicated pool, <1% fallback
Dedicated Silver | 150ms | 400ms | dedicated pool, <0.5% fallback
```

sophie: I'll start a doc in the GH repo: /docs/pricing/dedicated-billing.md and add billing scenarios like: monthly reserved + burst hours, proration on mid-cycle downgrades, and credits example. Will link back here when skeleton is ready.

kevin: I'll draft runbooks and a short escalation matrix. For credits: propose internal owner = support manager, external owner = account rep. Timeline: credit request validated within 7 business days, payout applied next invoice.

lili: I'll review Ajay's RFC and Kevin's credit flow. Also need to confirm any regulatory constraints for customers in EU with private deployments — may need separate SLA/cap.

ops-bot: Created tentative GA-gate sync event: Thu 10:00–10:30 (calendar: https://calendar.example.com/event/ga-gate-sync). Invited: maria, ajay, sophie, kevin, lili.

maria: Thanks — if everyone can drop their drafts into the shared drive (links in the calendar invite) before the meeting we can finalize acceptance criteria and gate checklist. Also +1 on explicit examples in docs so CS and sales can use them in customer conversations. :thumbsup:

kevin: Quick follow-up — can we include a short table in the public-facing docs that maps incident severity -> expected response time -> compensation path? That will cut down back-and-forth with customers.

sophie: Good idea. I'll add a compact "SLA at a glance" table for external docs and a more detailed internal runbook for support.

maria: OK locking this thread as the working tracker for drafts. If anyone needs more time call it out here. Otherwise see you at Thu sync.

ajay: FYI I'll call out streaming vs blocking inference separately in the RFC — they should have different SLOs.

lili: FYI I'll likely ask finance for a mock of the worst-case credit impact so we can set the cap rationally.

kevin: +1. I'll include the operational cost model for incident mitigation (e.g., burst capacity costs) in the runbook so sales understands tradeoffs.

maria: Great — thanks all.

ops-bot: Reminder: GA-gate sync Thu 10:00 — 24h
